question: As a British citizen or permanent resident, which TWO responsibilities do you have? Select two.
romanUrdu: British citizen ya permanent resident ke tor par aap ki do zimmedariyan kya hain?

choices.text: To look after yourself and your family
To serve in the armed forces
To attend a place of worship every week

explanation: The handbook lists respecting and obeying the law, and looking after yourself and your family, among the responsibilities of residents and citizens. Serving in the armed forces and weekly worship are not listed as responsibilities.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 1.3 The values and principles of the UK: responsibilities of residents and citizens

question: Who made the first coins to be minted in Britain?
romanUrdu: Britain mein sab se pehle sikke kisne banaye?

choices.text: The people of the Iron Age

explanation: The people of the Iron Age made the first coins to be minted in Britain, some inscribed with the names of Iron Age kings.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.7 Early Britain: the Iron Age

question: Who first built the Tower of London?
romanUrdu: Tower of London sab se pehle kisne banaya?
explanation: The Tower of London was first built by William the Conqueror after he became king in 1066. Its White Tower is a Norman castle keep built on his orders.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 4.5 Places of interest: the Tower of London

question: There are 15 national parks in England, Wales and Scotland. What are national parks?
romanUrdu: England, Wales aur Scotland mein 15 national parks hain. National parks kya hain?

choices.text: Private estates closed to the public
Nature reserves where nobody may live
Areas of protected countryside that everyone can visit

explanation: The handbook describes the 15 national parks as areas of protected countryside that everyone can visit, and where people live, work and look after the landscape.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 4.5 Places of interest: national parks

question: Does Northern Ireland have its own established church?
romanUrdu: Kya Northern Ireland ka apna established church hai?

choices.text: Yes, the Presbyterian Church is the established church
Yes, the Church of Ireland is the established church
Yes, the Roman Catholic Church is the established church
No, there is no established church in Northern Ireland

explanation: The handbook states that there is no established Church in Wales or Northern Ireland. The Church of England is the established church in England only.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 4.6 Religion: churches in the UK

question: Which three territories make up Great Britain?
romanUrdu: Great Britain kaunse teen ilaqon se banta hai?

choices.text: England, Wales and the Republic of Ireland

explanation: Great Britain refers only to England, Scotland and Wales, not to Northern Ireland.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 2.2 What is the UK?

question: How often are Prime Minister's Questions held while Parliament is sitting?
romanUrdu: Jab Parliament ka ijlas ho raha ho to Prime Minister's Questions kitni baar hoti hain?
explanation: Prime Minister's Questions takes place every week while Parliament is sitting. It is an important opportunity for the leader of the opposition to challenge the government.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 5.6 The government: the opposition

question: Which king was executed in 1649?
romanUrdu: 1649 mein kis badshah ko qatl kiya gaya?
explanation: Charles I was held prisoner after his army was defeated, refused to reach agreement with Parliament, and was executed in 1649. England then declared itself a republic.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.6 The Tudors and Stuarts: Oliver Cromwell and the English Republic

question: Where was William Shakespeare born?
romanUrdu: William Shakespeare kahan paida hue?
explanation: Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon, England. He was a playwright and actor who wrote many poems and plays.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.6 The Tudors and Stuarts: William Shakespeare

question: Which TWO of the following are famous British Paralympians? Select two.
romanUrdu: In mein se kaun do mashhoor British Paralympians hain?
explanation: Baroness Tanni Grey-Thompson won 16 Paralympic medals in wheelchair racing, and Ellie Simmonds won Paralympic swimming golds in 2008 and 2012. Kelly Holmes and Steve Redgrave were Olympic champions, not Paralympians.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 4.7 Sport: notable British sportsmen and women

question: Who was reigning in England when English settlers first began to colonise the eastern coast of America?
romanUrdu: Jab English settlers ne America ke mashriqi sahil par colony banana shuru ki, us waqt England mein kaun hukumat kar raha tha?
explanation: In Elizabeth I's time, English settlers first began to colonise the eastern coast of America. This colonisation greatly increased in the next century.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.6 The Tudors and Stuarts: exploration, poetry and drama

question: Under the individual registration system used in Northern Ireland, must voters complete their own registration form?
romanUrdu: Northern Ireland mein individual registration system ke tehat kya voters ko apna registration form khud bharna hota hai?

choices.text: No, one form is completed for the whole household
Only people who own their home must complete one
No, the local council completes it for them
Yes, each person entitled to vote must complete their own form

explanation: In Northern Ireland, individual registration applies: all those entitled to vote must complete their own registration form. Elsewhere in the UK a form is sent to every household.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 5.6.1 Who can vote? (Northern Ireland: individual registration)

question: On which day is the birth of Jesus Christ celebrated?
romanUrdu: Jesus Christ ki paidaish kis din manai jati hai?
explanation: Christmas Day, 25 December, celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ and is a public holiday.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 4.3 Customs and traditions: the main Christian festivals

question: What sort of battle was the Battle of Britain, fought between Germany and Britain in the summer of 1940?
romanUrdu: 1940 ki garmiyon mein Germany aur Britain ke darmiyan lari gayi Battle of Britain kaisi jang thi?

choices.text: A tank battle fought on land
A naval battle fought at sea
An aerial battle fought in the air

explanation: Germany waged an air campaign against Britain, but the British resisted with fighter planes and won the crucial aerial battle called the Battle of Britain in the summer of 1940.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.4 The 20th century: the Second World War (the Battle of Britain)

question: Where is Swansea located?
romanUrdu: Swansea kahan waqia hai?
explanation: Swansea is a city in Wales, listed with Cardiff and Newport among the cities of Wales.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 4.8 The UK today: cities of the UK (Wales)

question: Which TWO political parties formed the coalition government in 2010? Select two.
romanUrdu: 2010 mein kaunsi do siyasi jamaaton ne coalition government banayi?
explanation: In May 2010 no political party won an overall majority, so the Conservative and Liberal Democrat parties formed a coalition and David Cameron became Prime Minister.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.2 Britain since 1945: coalition government from 2010 to 2015

question: Who established the Church of England?
romanUrdu: Church of England kisne qaim ki?
explanation: When the Pope refused to approve his divorce, Henry VIII established the Church of England, in which the king rather than the Pope appointed bishops. Elizabeth I later re-established it as the official Church in England.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.6 The Tudors and Stuarts: Henry VIII

question: In 1348, one third of the population of England, Wales and Scotland died as a result of which disease?
romanUrdu: 1348 mein England, Wales aur Scotland ki ek tihai abadi kis bimari se mari?
explanation: In 1348 a disease, probably a form of plague, came to Britain and became known as the Black Death. One third of the population of England died, with a similar proportion in Scotland and Wales.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.5 The Middle Ages: the Black Death

question: Haggis is a traditional food from which part of the UK?
romanUrdu: Haggis UK ke kis hisse ka riwati khana hai?
explanation: Haggis, a sheep's stomach stuffed with offal, suet, onions and oatmeal, is the traditional food associated with Scotland.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 4.4 Leisure: traditional foods

question: Which court deals with minor criminal offences in Scotland?
romanUrdu: Scotland mein halki criminal offences kaunsi adalat sunti hai?

choices.text: The Justice of the Peace Court

explanation: In Scotland, minor criminal offences go to a Justice of the Peace Court. Magistrates' Courts deal with minor criminal cases in England, Wales and Northern Ireland.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 5.5 Respecting the law: Magistrates' and Justice of the Peace Courts

question: Which TWO records give us information about England during the reign of William the Conqueror? Select two.
romanUrdu: William the Conqueror ke daur mein England ke bare mein kaunse do record maloomat dete hain?
explanation: The Bayeux Tapestry commemorates William's victory at the Battle of Hastings, and the Domesday Book lists the towns, villages, people, land and animals of England just after the Norman Conquest.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.7 Early Britain: the Norman Conquest and the Domesday Book

question: In 1913 the British government promised Home Rule for Ireland. Why were changes delayed until 1921?
romanUrdu: 1913 mein British government ne Ireland ke liye Home Rule ka wada kiya. Tabdeeliyan 1921 tak kyun multawi rahin?

choices.text: The outbreak of the First World War in 1914
The outbreak of the Second World War in 1939

explanation: The outbreak of the First World War led the British government to postpone any changes in Ireland. A peace treaty was signed in 1921 and Ireland became two countries in 1922.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.4 The 20th century: the partition of Ireland

question: Which statement about Queen Elizabeth I is true?
romanUrdu: Queen Elizabeth I ke bare mein kaunsa bayan durust hai?

choices.text: She was a Protestant and balanced the views of Catholics and more extreme Protestants
She was a Catholic and restored the Pope's authority in England
She was a Puritan and banned all other forms of worship
She was a Presbyterian and made the Church of Scotland a state church

explanation: Elizabeth I was a Protestant. She re-established the Church of England and succeeded in finding a balance between the views of Catholics and the more extreme Protestants, avoiding serious religious conflict in England.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 3.6 The Tudors and Stuarts: Queen Elizabeth I

question: Which TWO documents do you need when applying for a National Insurance number? Select two.
romanUrdu: National Insurance number ke liye apply karte waqt kaunse do documents chahiye?

choices.text: A reference from a previous employer
Documents that prove you have permission to work in the UK
A tenancy agreement for your home

explanation: The handbook says you will usually need documents that prove your identity and that you have permission to work in the UK. A National Insurance number does not on its own prove to an employer that you have the right to work.

sources.title: Life in the UK: A guide for new residents, 3rd edition
sources.locator: 5.4.1 Taxation: getting a National Insurance number
